verdicts.reason: The account holds Rs 909,657 (~79% of the disputed amount), well above the quarter-of-disputed threshold. A full pass-through ratio with only 1 payer and 1 payee, plus 200 shared devices/phones, strongly undercuts the registered-merchant status and supports the lien on the traced victim funds.

The lien of Rs 57,053 targets only the pro-rata traced victim money in an account with a negligible tainted share (0.007%), so the customer's own funds are not frozen. All other signals (low pass-through, high age, high transaction volume, no mule links) confirm the account is genuine, but it still holds a traceable portion of the victim's money.

The lien of Rs 23,484 covers only the traced victim funds in an account with a tainted share of ~4%, so the customer's own balance is unaffected. The account is a registered merchant with a long history and slow forwarding, consistent with genuine use, but the victim's money is still present per the trace.

The lien of Rs 21,878 freezes only the traced victim portion in an account with a ~2.9% tainted share, leaving the customer's own funds untouched. Low pass-through, long account age, no mule links, and high inflow count confirm legitimate use, but the traced victim money remains recoverable.

The lien of Rs 14,651 targets only the victim's traced money in an account with a negligible tainted share (0.11%), so the customer's own funds are not impacted. All signals (very low pass-through, 55 inflows, no mule connections) are consistent with a legitimate business.

The lien of Rs 11,676 freezes only the traced victim money in a very old account (2733 days) with a tainted share of just 0.54%, so the customer's own balance is not at risk. Nine distinct payers and near-zero pass-through confirm genuine use, but the victim's funds remain present per the trace.
